business_problem: CYRAN needed to deliver interactive geospatial intelligence in air-gapped and sovereign environments, but JPEG 2000 decode latency on large satellite scenes was the bottleneck that kept edge analytics from being practical.
solution_summary: CYRAN reworked the slowest stage of its SpatialFuse geospatial pipeline around NVIDIA DGX Spark rather than trying to push ever-larger scenes through traditional CPU or discrete-GPU workstations. The company built PixelFlux on top of nvJPEG2000 so compressed satellite imagery can be decoded directly on the GPU, and DGX Spark's unified memory means those buffers are immediately available to the CPU and downstream analytics without PCIe copy overhead. SpatialFuse then uses the decoded scenes for edge inference across orbit, air, and ground data sources in secure environments where cloud round-trips are not acceptable. DALI integration keeps the GPU fed from local storage for training and inference pipelines, and the same architecture now gives CYRAN a path from local edge validation to larger Blackwell-based cloud or data-center deployments without rewriting the core geospatial stack.

data_flow: Compressed satellite scenes enter PixelFlux, which uses nvJPEG2000 on DGX Spark to decode large JPEG 2000 imagery directly into unified memory. SpatialFuse then fuses those decoded scenes with other sensor inputs and serves geospatial analysis locally in air-gapped or forward-deployed environments.
business_outcome: CYRAN cut decode time on a 26 GB satellite scene from more than five minutes to just over two minutes, outperformed a CPU baseline by about 3x and a discrete GPU workstation by up to 2x, and made genuinely interactive geospatial analysis possible on local hardware without cloud dependency.

Interactive large-scene analysis runs entirely on local hardware-enabling air-gapped and sovereign intelligence deployments.
The first was GPU-accelerated JPEG 2000 decode. NVIDIA nvJPEG2000 moves the most computationally demanding stages of image decoding off the CPU and onto the GPU.
